source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

govt_capex.evidence: Bosch's tractor segment and Powertrain Solutions division saw 5.8% growth driven by tractor segment and export sales in FY2024-25, indicating indirect exposure to agricultural/infrastructure capex but no specific government capex revenue percentage disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Automotive PLI scheme (budgetary outlay Rs. 25,938 crore, FY2023-24 to FY2027-28) covers auto components; Bosch India's participation as a named PLI beneficiary was not confirmed in available public disclosures.

rural.evidence: Rural demand outpacing urban; continued expansion and deepening of rural and small-town distribution networks has enabled Pidilite to consistently outgrow urban markets, capitalizing on rise in rural consumption and lower category penetration. Specific revenue percentage not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: VAM (Vinyl Acetate Monomer), a derivative of crude oil, is a key raw material for Pidilite's adhesives; company meets VAM requirement largely via imports. Exact % of total RM costs not disclosed in public summaries.

rate_sensitive.evidence: ABSLAMC is an asset management company; interest rate changes materially affect fixed income/debt AUM. As of Q4 FY25, Equity MF QAAUM was 44% of total MF QAAUM (Rs. 1,691 billion of Rs. 3,817 billion), implying ~56% is debt/liquid/passive. Rising rates typically cause debt fund AUM outflows, impacting management fee revenue. Floating rate liability % of company's own debt not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Global pharma companies diversifying away from China; India's CDMO market projected to grow from USD 3.5 billion to USD 25 billion over next decade. Lupin Manufacturing Solutions (LMS) is strategically positioned with differentiated model, dedicated capacities, and quality-first operations to become a preferred global API CDMO partner — indicative of China+1 positioning without explicit attribution of specific revenue.

inr_exposure.evidence: US revenue for FY2025 was USD 925 million (~38% of global sales), making Lupin significantly exposed to USD/INR movements. Hedging policy details not confirmed in public summaries.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin is confirmed as a PLI scheme beneficiary (pharma PLI for APIs/KSMs). Pharmaceutical sector secured Rs. 2,328 crore in PLI disbursements in FY25 with Lupin among named beneficiaries. Specific Lupin revenue or income from PLI not separately quantified in public disclosures.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company has ~68% export revenue with significant Asia presence (42% of total revenue), but no explicit China+1 narrative or attribution of export growth to China diversification found in available FY2025 disclosures.

inr_exposure.evidence: US generics revenue was Rs. 1,047 crore (~23% of total FY25 revenue of Rs. 4,648 crore). Additional USD exposure likely from Africa and some Asian markets. Specific hedging policy not confirmed in public summaries.

rural.evidence: Rural demand cited as positive driver for RE motorcycles; management highlighted rural uptick aided by GST cuts on motorcycles below 350cc and government consumption measures, but no specific rural revenue % disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: VECV (commercial vehicles) benefits indirectly from infrastructure capex driving truck demand; no specific government capex revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Eicher Motors is largely debt-free at the standalone level; no specific floating rate liability % disclosed in available sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Steel and aluminium are primary raw materials for motorcycles and trucks; crude-linked inputs (plastics, rubber) also relevant but no specific % of raw materials disclosed in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: International motorcycle sales constituted ~12.5% of Royal Enfield's total turnover in FY25 (100,136 units exported out of 1,002,893 total); geographic presence in UK, USA, Europe, SE Asia through subsidiaries.

china_plus_one.evidence: JB Chemicals sources APIs and intermediates but no explicit China+1 narrative found in available FY25 disclosures; API segment revenue is only Rs 76 Cr (2% of revenue), limiting direct China API exposure narrative.

rural.evidence: Domestic formulations (55% of revenue) include branded Rx and OTC products distributed through hospitals, retail chemists, and rural health infrastructure, but no specific rural revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: JB Chemicals has modest debt levels; specific floating rate liability % not disclosed in available sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Pharmaceutical raw materials include APIs and intermediates; crude-linked solvents are used but no specific % of crude-linked raw materials to total raw materials disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: International segment (export formulations + CDMO) contributed 42% of FY25 revenue (Rs 1,574 Cr out of Rs 3,918 Cr); exports to Russia, South Africa, USA and branded generics markets.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmation of JB Chemicals being a PLI scheme beneficiary found in available FY25 sources; API segment is very small (Rs 76 Cr, 2% of revenue).

rural.evidence: Mass brands (8PM Whisky, Magic Moments Vodka, Contessa Rum) distributed through 100,000+ retail outlets and 10,000 on-premise outlets pan-India; Regular & Others segment represents 53.9% of IMFL volumes in FY25; no specific rural revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company mentions interest rate risk in forward-looking statements but specific floating rate liability % not disclosed in available sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA) from grain/molasses, glass bottles, and packaging; not crude-linked directly. Grain and ENA prices were described as stable in FY25.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports to over 100 countries represent 9% of FY25 IMFL sales value; key international presence in Dubai, USA, UK, Singapore; Rampur Single Malt available in ~50 countries.

rural.evidence: Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities cited as key strategic growth area; physical store network expanded to 237 stores in 79 cities (FY2025) including Indore, Jaipur, Lucknow, Bhubaneswar; 9 million new customers acquired in FY25 with significant share from Tier 2/3; no specific revenue % by city tier disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt ~Rs 990 Cr; company actively reducing debt; primarily funded through working capital borrowings which are typically floating rate; specific floating rate % not disclosed in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Purely domestic e-commerce platform; no export revenue; no meaningful USD revenue exposure.

china_plus_one.evidence: Sun Pharma has strong backward integration with 14 API manufacturing facilities producing 400+ APIs in-house, which provides supply chain resilience; however no explicit China+1 narrative found in FY25 MD&A; company is a net exporter of APIs to 60+ countries.

rural.evidence: India domestic formulations (33% of revenue, Rs 16,923 Cr in FY25, +13.7% YoY) sold through retail pharmacies and hospitals including rural health infrastructure; no specific rural revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Sun Pharma is largely cash-rich/net debt-free at consolidated level; specific floating rate liability % not available from sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Pharmaceutical raw materials (APIs, solvents, packaging) partially crude-linked; company has backward integration for APIs reducing external raw material dependency; no specific crude-linked % of raw materials disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: US formulations: 31% of FY25 revenue ($1,921M, +3.6% YoY); Emerging markets: 18% ($1,114M, +7% YoY); ROW: 14% ($847M, +4.5% YoY); API & Others: 4%; total international ~67% of Rs 52,041 Cr consolidated revenue.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries was among 16 companies selected under PLI scheme for promotion of domestic manufacturing of critical KSMs/Drug Intermediates and APIs; scheme approved by Union Cabinet on 24.02.2021; specific PLI incentive revenue received not disclosed in available FY25 sources.

rural.evidence: Company expanding presence in Tier-III and Tier-IV cities; operated 298 clinical labs and 6,607 Patient Service Centers as of March 31, 2025. Delhi-NCR ~31% of revenues, North India (ex-NCR) ~31%, East and West ~15% each, South ~6%. No specific rural revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is nearly debt-free. Total debt minimal (~Rs 200 Cr book value); interest expense ~Rs 22 Cr in FY25. No material floating rate exposure disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: No foreign currency revenue; purely domestic INR business.
inr_exposure.evidence: Dr Lal PathLabs is a purely domestic diagnostic services company with no export revenue.

china_plus_one.evidence: Caplin Point focuses on LATAM branded generics. API sourcing: ~45% outsourced (of which ~30% from China, ~70% from Indian vendors); ~55% manufactured in-house. No explicit China+1 diversification narrative present in available disclosures.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is near debt-free. Total debt ~Rs 4.9 million (de minimis) as of FY25; no material floating rate exposure.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: No hedging. Company explicitly does not enter into derivative contracts. Currency risk managed by keeping goods in inventory in local-currency markets; price increases used to offset currency losses on receivables.
inr_exposure.evidence: Foreign exchange earned FY25: INR 720 crore (exports). Company stated it does not go for any hedging and does not enter into any derivatives contracts.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme participation identified. Caplin Point is a formulations exporter focused on LATAM; PLI pharma scheme targets domestic API/formulation manufacturers.

china_plus_one.evidence: Supply chain diversification trends (including China+1 strategies by multinationals) are boosting direct engagements and export opportunities for Indian specialty chemical makers like Navin Fluorine, evidenced by strategic global partnerships (e.g., Chemours, Buss ChemTech). Export regions include North America, Europe, Middle East, and Asia Pacific. No explicit China+1 attribution of specific revenue in AR.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw material is fluorspar (fluorite), not crude oil. Company does not have direct crude oil exposure.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports accounted for 56% of FY25 revenue (Rs 2,349 Cr total revenue). Export geographies: North America, Europe, Middle East, Asia Pacific.

pli_scheme.evidence: Navin Fluorine has been identified as a potential beneficiary of India's PLI scheme for specialty chemicals/fluoropolymers. Company has rapid capacity additions in fluoropolymers. Specific PLI approval or revenue from PLI not confirmed in available disclosures.

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB India follows a 'local-for-local' strategy with >85% domestic revenue. No China+1 narrative in available disclosures. Company serves domestic power, railways, data centers, cement markets.

govt_capex.evidence: ABB India has 35-40% indirect exposure to government capex (infrastructure, railways, power sector). CY2024 order inflow of Rs 13,079 Cr impacted by weak government orders. Policy-driven public sector capex in energy transition, FDI in steel/cement, PLI in specialty steel and battery manufacturing cited as key opportunity drivers.

rate_sensitive.evidence: ABB India is effectively debt-free (cash-rich balance sheet). No significant floating rate debt exposure.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports account for ~10% of revenue (serves 30+ countries). Revenue predominantly in INR. Forex volatility cited as risk in Q2 CY2025, with 20% PAT decline partly attributed to forex impact.

pli_scheme.evidence: ABB India is not a direct PLI scheme beneficiary. However, the company benefits indirectly as customers in PLI-linked sectors (specialty steel, battery manufacturing) increase capex.

china_plus_one.evidence: Global pharma companies shifting CRO/CDMO work from China to India is a core thesis. Company serves 300+ innovator pharma and biotech companies across US, UK, Europe, and Japan. Analysts cite 'global China+1 CRDMO supercycle narrative' as key driver. Company positioned as 'India's WuXi' alternative. Revenue from overseas customers: 97.95% in FY24 and ~98% in FY25.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company completed planned Rs 720 Cr debt repayment in FY25, significantly strengthening balance sheet. Post-IPO and repayment, debt significantly reduced. Specific floating rate % not disclosed in available sources.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedge through USD/EUR revenue against INR cost base. Almost all revenue is in USD/EUR while costs are in INR. Formal hedging policy details not available from public sources.
inr_exposure.evidence: Overseas customers contributed 97.95% of FY24 revenue (Rs 1,438.60 Cr of total) and ~98% in FY25. US and Europe are dominant markets.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme participation identified. Sai Life Sciences is a CRO/CDMO company; pharma PLI scheme targets bulk drug (API) domestic manufacturers, not contract research organizations.

rural.evidence: Officer's Choice (world's 3rd largest whisky brand) is the dominant mass-market volume brand. Popular and mass-premium segments drive majority of 33.1 million cases sold in FY2025. Prestige & Above (P&A) at 47.2% of volumes and 57.3% of sales value, implying mass/popular segment is ~52.8% of volumes. Specific rural revenue percentage not disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: CSD (Canteen Stores Department — army/defence retail channel) is a distribution channel for ABDL products. Specific CSD revenue percentage not disclosed in FY2025 annual report public disclosures.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Credit rating upgraded from IND BBB+ to IND A- with positive outlook in FY2025; significant improvement in net debt profile and leverage ratios. Specific floating/fixed rate debt split not disclosed in available sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA) and glass bottles/packaging. ENA prices linked to agricultural commodity prices (sugarcane/molasses), not crude oil. No petroleum-linked raw material identified.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue grew ~16% YoY to Rs 206 crore in FY2025, representing ~6% of net revenue of ~Rs 3,441 crore. Specific hedging policy details not disclosed in available public sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme applicable to Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) sector. No PLI beneficiary status mentioned in FY2025 disclosures.

rural.evidence: India domestic business (55% of revenue, Rs 6,393 crore in FY2025, up 13% YoY) operates through branded generics model covering both urban and rural markets. No specific rural revenue percentage disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Specific floating vs fixed rate debt split not found in publicly available FY2025 annual report disclosures. Company had significant debt taken on for acquisitions (Elder Pharma, Curatio).

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are APIs and intermediates. No significant crude oil direct raw material exposure. Some solvents may be petrochemical-derived but not material.

inr_exposure.evidence: US revenue Rs 1,100 crore (10% of Rs 11,516 crore total); Brazil Rs ~1,100 crore (10%); other ROW ~15%. Total non-India revenue ~45%. US revenues denominated in USD; Germany in EUR; Brazil in BRL. Estimated USD-denominated revenue ~20% of total (US + some ROW).

pli_scheme.evidence: Torrent Pharmaceuticals manufactures APIs and formulations in India. Pharma PLI scheme covers both APIs and formulations. Explicit beneficiary confirmation and PLI revenue contribution not confirmed in publicly available FY2025 annual report sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: KSB India is being established as a key global manufacturing hub for the KSB Group, with exports recording 22% CAGR and constituting 17% of total revenue in 2025. Export orders from Middle East (KSB Pumps Arabia UAE water order) and North Africa (Hassi Massoud Refinery, Algeria). India positioning as global manufacturing base — implicit China+1 dynamic for the KSB Group, but no explicit 'China+1' text found in publicly available disclosures.

govt_capex.evidence: Significant government-linked revenues: solar pump orders of INR 58 crore from government departments (Dept of Horticulture Rajasthan, Maharashtra State Electricity, MPUVNL, DGVCL); water segment driven by government irrigation, drinking water supply and sanitation projects; landmark supercritical power plant order. Government/infrastructure is a major end-user segment but specific percentage not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: KSB manufactures pumps and valves — primary inputs are castings (grey iron, stainless steel), forgings, and bought-out components. No crude oil raw material exposure identified.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports constitute 17% of total revenue (Rs ~458 crore of Rs 2,696 crore total). Export markets include Middle East and Africa. Revenue denominated in USD and local currencies.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme applicable to pumps and valves manufacturing sector. No PLI beneficiary status mentioned in available disclosures.

rural.evidence: Shyam Metalics produces TMT bars, wire rods, and other long steel products that serve housing and construction including rural markets. No specific rural revenue percentage disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Management commentary cites government-driven infrastructure demand (railways, roads, gas pipelines, urban housing, defence, engineering) as key steel demand driver. Specific government revenue percentage not disclosed in FY2025 public disclosures.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are iron ore, coking coal (metallurgical coal, imported), and scrap metal. Coking coal price linked to global coal markets, not crude oil. No petroleum-linked raw material identified as significant input.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company exports to approximately 25 countries (ferroalloys, pellets). Dubai subsidiary (SMIDMCC) was liquidated during FY2025. Specific export revenue percentage not disclosed in publicly available FY2025 annual report sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Steel and metals sector is not covered under the PLI scheme. No PLI beneficiary status mentioned in FY2025 disclosures.

china_plus_one.evidence: Export order booking grew 51% to Rs 10.19 billion in FY2025, constituting 54% of total order booking. Company operates across 75+ countries with subsidiaries in UK, Dubai, and South Africa. Key export markets include Middle East, Europe, and Southeast Asia. India's domestic market share in sub-100MW turbines rose to ~55%. Export momentum and global manufacturing positioning indicate India emerging as alternative supply source for industrial steam turbines — but no explicit 'China+1' text found in publicly available FY2025 MD&A.

govt_capex.evidence: Products include industrial captive power, co-generation, waste heat recovery, and biomass/renewable energy turbines for industries. Government-backed renewable energy (biomass, waste-to-energy) and industrial policy drives demand. No direct government contract revenue percentage disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Triveni Turbine is effectively debt-free with strong cash generation. Specific floating/fixed rate debt split not applicable or disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary inputs are castings, forgings, and precision machined components (steel-based). No crude oil raw material exposure identified.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export sales were Rs 9.67 billion (~48% of FY2025 total revenue of Rs 20.06 billion). Export markets include Middle East, Europe, Africa, and Southeast Asia — primarily USD and EUR denominated.

pli_scheme.evidence: Management has indicated interest in PLI support for energy storage solutions (CO2 and air expansion turbines) but no confirmed PLI beneficiary status for core steam turbine products in FY2025. Standard industrial steam turbines are not covered under current PLI schemes.
